OSPS-AC-01.01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default. The repository baseline script sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege and review routing goes through CODEOWNERS to the `owners` team; the settings are code, applied and drift-checked by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: Untrusted workflow metadata is validated before use: the shared workflows accept inputs against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the pinned publish stub shape checked by lint:release-stub), and zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns where untrusted context would reach a shell.
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: This is the project's central architectural rule, not an incidental setting: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may declare `id-token: write`. lint:capability-boundary enforces it in the gate and fails the build if a `workflow_call` workflow ever acquires the privileged identity, so a certificate bearing this repository's identity can never be minted by a job executing a caller's code.
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: Collaborator-supplied input is validated rather than trusted: workflow inputs are checked against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the release-stub shape), and zizmor fails the gate on any pattern that would interpolate untrusted context into a shell.
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Every release is a unique semantic version, derived from conventional commits by git-cliff and tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch> by the release App; the tag ruleset makes tags immutable, so a version identifier is never reused.
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Verified on the published release: assets are named for the release identifier (github-1.22.2.tar.gz, github-1.22.2.spdx.json) and each is additionally bound by cryptographic digest in checksums.txt and in the attestations.intoto.jsonl evidence bundle, so the association survives a rename. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/releases/tag/v1.22.2
OSPS-BR-03.01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, releases, documentation and issue tracker are all served by GitHub over TLS, and no plaintext URI appears in the tree.
OSPS-BR-03.02_justification: Distribution is over HTTPS and authenticated beyond transport: releases carry Sigstore evidence bundles and GitHub artifact attestations, and every consumed tool is pinned with per-platform checksums in mise.lock, so a substituted artifact fails verification rather than merely a certificate check.
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: CHANGELOG.md is generated by git-cliff from conventional commits and the same descriptive log is attached to each GitHub release, so functional and security modifications are recorded per release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/releases
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised: mise with an exact-version config and a lockfile carrying per-platform checksums for tools, and the language-native managers (cargo, npm) for consuming repositories. Preference is for aqua-backed tools so downloads carry checksums and attestations rather than running install scripts.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: Each release carries a Sigstore evidence bundle and GitHub artifact attestations covering every published asset by cryptographic digest, and docs/runbook.md documents how a consumer verifies them. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
OSPS-DO-01.01_justification: README.md documents basic usage for consumers (adopt the gate in about six lines, copy scaffold/, run `mise run ci`), and docs/runbook.md is the full operating manual for wiring a repository in and for recovery. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: docs/runbook.md has a section written from the consumer's position — 'Verifying as a consumer would' — giving the commands to check a release's attestations and Sigstore evidence bundle against the published digests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: The same documentation covers authorship identity, which in a keyless design is the workflow identity: verification checks the signer's workflow ref in the certificate rather than a personal key, and the release tooling exposes an explicit signer-workflow flag so a consumer can assert which identity must have signed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: There is no written statement of support scope or duration per release. In practice consumers pin a tag or SHA and the newest release is the supported one, but MAINTENANCE.md documents the compatibility surface without saying how long any release is supported. A short support statement would close this and osps_do_05_01 together.
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: There is no published end-of-life statement saying when a release stops receiving security updates. It follows the same gap as osps_do_04_01.
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md give the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings every required tool at its pinned version from the lockfile, and `mise run ci` then runs exactly what CI runs. There are no separate libraries, frameworks or SDKs to install. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: Roles are not described as roles. docs/continuity.md names who holds which sensitive asset and CODEOWNERS routes review to an `owners` team, but there is no document defining the project's roles and what each is responsible for. It is the same gap as the Silver `roles_responsibilities` and `governance` criteria, and one document would close all three.
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests are open for public discussion of proposed changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and individually addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
OSPS-GV-03.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: There is no written policy requiring that a collaborator be reviewed before being granted escalated permissions to sensitive resources. In practice there is one maintainer and permissions are assigned explicitly rather than by default, but the policy itself is unwritten — the same documentation gap as the governance and roles criteria.
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: The released assets carry the same 0BSD licence as the source; there is no separate licence for releases. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-03.01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, the REUSE-standard location. api.reuse.software independently reports the project compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-03.02_justification: Released assets ship from this repository, which carries LICENSE at its root and LICENSES/0BSD.txt alongside, with per-file attribution recorded in REUSE.toml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-QA-01.01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github
OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: mise/config.toml lists every direct tool dependency at an exact version, and mise.lock records per-platform checksums for each. Renovate reads the same file natively. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/mise/config.toml
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: Every release ships an SPDX software bill of materials as a release asset — verified on v1.22.2: github-1.22.2.spdx.json, alongside github-1.22.2.tar.gz, checksums.txt and the attestations.intoto.jsonl evidence bundle. The SBOM is generated by the release pipeline (release/generate-sbom.sh) rather than hand-maintained. Previously answered N/A on the grounds that this repository compiles nothing; that was technically available but less true than the facts — the SBOM is published regardless. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/releases/tag/v1.22.2
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: The organisation's repositories and their status are documented rather than assumed: docs/migration-playbook.md records which codebases join the governance and how, and the scheduled audit enumerates the live repository population from the GitHub API rather than from a hand-kept list. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/migration-playbook.md
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: A release of this project comprises this single source repository; there are no subprojects releasing alongside it. Other repositories in the organisation consume this one's governance, which is by construction as strict or stricter.
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed. The repository contains shell tasks, workflow YAML, configuration and documentation; tools arrive at runtime through mise from pinned, checksummed downloads rather than being vendored.
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed — every tracked file is text and reviewable in a diff.
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: gate.yml runs the full automated suite — `mise run ci`, every belt check against every tracked file — on each pull request before it can be accepted, and it does so by self-applying the reusable workflow this project publishes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: Documented in both places a reader would look: README.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs, and CONTRIBUTING.md makes a green gate a requirement for every change. When they run is equally explicit — on every pull request and every push to main, with the network-bound checks on a Monday schedule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: The practice is followed — recent changes each shipped the check that holds them — and the rule is written in CLAUDE.md, but it is not stated as a policy in the contributor-facing documentation. The same missing sentence as the Silver `tests_documented_added` and `test_policy_mandated` criteria.
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: docs/release.md specifies the pipeline actor by actor and action by action — what each workflow does, which identity it runs as, what it is permitted to touch — and docs/build-track.md and docs/source-track.md carry the per-track designs. The capability boundary between caller code and the privileged identity is stated explicitly as a design rule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/release.md
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: The external interfaces are the reusable workflows and the task contract: docs/runbook.md documents each workflow's inputs and the artifact classes with their required parameters, and workflow-templates/ ships a caller stub per workflow. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: Vulnerability data is published rather than held privately: resolved reports would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on the repository, and the dependency track already publishes machine-readable VEX decisions keyed by package and version for the advisories that touch this project's dependencies. No vulnerability in this project's own code has been discovered to date. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: Exactly this: the dependency track emits VEX documents keyed by package@version recording non-exploitability decisions for advisories that do not affect the project, with coverage derived rather than asserted, and the release path refuses to publish while an advisory in the SBOM is undecided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: docs/dependency-track.md defines the thresholds: cargo-deny bans and licence rules are deterministic and fail the gate, sources are restricted to a single registry with unknown-registry and unknown-git denied, and every advisory must exit through an explicit decision rather than being left open. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: Automatically, on every change: cargo-deny runs deterministically in the gate over the lockfile and the committed deny.toml, dependency-review runs on every pull request, and Renovate and Dependabot raise updates as advisories land. The policy those checks enforce is written in docs/dependency-track.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: There is no written remediation threshold for static-analysis findings. In practice the threshold is zero — any finding fails the gate and a red gate cannot merge — but that is a property of the machinery rather than a documented policy, and writing it down is what this criterion asks for.
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: Every change is automatically evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and trivy run in the gate, which is a required status check that a pull request cannot merge past. The requirement that the gate pass is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md; what is missing is only a stated severity threshold, recorded honestly under osps_vm_06_01. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md are the written assurance case, and docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md assess each claim against its evidence: the threat model (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, tampered artifacts), the countermeasures (the capability boundary, SHA pinning with checksums and attestations, keyless signing with transparency-log evidence), and an explicit record of what is NOT claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
build_floss_tools_justification: No build step exists (see the build criterion).
build_preserve_debug_justification: No build or installation system exists.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, in the standard location, and served as the organisation default to every repository in the org. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: There is no document stating how code review is conducted, what a reviewer must check and what makes a change acceptable. CONTRIBUTING.md states the mechanical requirements a change must satisfy and the gate enforces them, but the review standard itself is unwritten — and with one maintainer there is no second reviewer to apply it. Worth writing alongside the governance document.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate: shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor, rumdl, typos and committed all run in `mise run ci` on every pull request, and `fix:*` siblings apply the machine-fixable subset. Style is never a review comment here.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gate as the coding standard in executable form, and the standards are specific per language: shellcheck for shell (with bash pinned by `[task_config] shell` because Ubuntu's sh is dash), actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML, rumdl for Markdown, typos for spelling with the locale registers written down, and Conventional Commits with a 72-column subject ceiling. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement, attached through REUSE.toml rather than as an inline comment in each file — the REUSE specification's supported mechanism for files that cannot carry headers. `reuse lint` reports 141 of 141 files with copyright information, and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project implements no cryptography and selects no algorithms; where cryptography is used it is Sigstore's and GitHub's, whose algorithm choices the project does not control.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations are delegated to software built for the purpose — Sigstore/cosign, GitHub's attestation tooling and git — never reimplemented here.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software stores no authentication credentials or private keys at all. Secrets live in GitHub environment and organisation secrets, never in files in the repository, and release signing uses ephemeral keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is implementable with FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git are open source.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no keylengths. Release signing uses ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements no key agreement protocol; it is configuration and workflows, not a network service.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Where it relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, SHA-256 checksums and OpenPGP-free keyless signing.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; release signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Integrity everywhere is SHA-256 — per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects — and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. No MD5 or SHA-1 is relied on as a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: artifact integrity uses SHA-256 (per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects) and signing uses Sigstore's ECDSA P-256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Everything is delivered over HTTPS by GitHub. Beyond transport, the toolbelt pins every tool by exact version with per-platform checksums in mise.lock and verifies GitHub attestations, and every uses: is pinned to a full commit SHA.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are not fetched over http at use time: they are committed in mise.lock in this repository and travel with the source, and releases additionally carry Sigstore evidence bundles.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, individually addressable by URL, open to new participants, and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/direction.md is the roadmap and it is unusually explicit about what the project will NOT do: a target table naming the level intended on each SLSA track, the claims policy, and the deliberate ceilings (BuildEnv is held at L0 by choice, Gold-level criteria are not claimed while there is one maintainer). Open items are tracked as issues and the table is the first thing a closing issue updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English (en-US in code and identifiers, en-GB in prose, a convention recorded in CLAUDE.md).
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are filed as issues, triaged, and either scheduled with a linked pull request or closed with the reason recorded; none are left unanswered.
floss_license_justification: Released under 0BSD, a FLOSS licence. LICENSE at the repository root, full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, per-file attribution via REUSE.toml, enforced in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: There is no GOVERNANCE document. Decision-making is in practice a single maintainer with a documented succession plan (docs/continuity.md) and CODEOWNERS routing, but the governance model itself — how decisions are made, who decides, how that changes — is not written down. This is a documentation gap, not a process one, and is the next thing to write.
input_validation_justification: The shared workflows validate their inputs against allowlists rather than trusting callers: the artifact `classes:` input accepts only a known set, the publish stub's filename and shape are checked by lint:release-stub, and workflow inputs that would otherwise be interpolated into shell are guarded — zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns.
interact_justification: The README links CONTRIBUTING.md (how to contribute), SUPPORT.md (how to get help) and SECURITY.md (how to report vulnerabilities); issue forms and a pull-request template are provided in .github/. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github
internationalization_justification: The software produced is shell tasks, workflows and configuration; it emits maintainer-facing diagnostics only and has no end-user interface strings to localise.
know_common_errors_justification: The documented threat reasoning covers the error classes specific to this software: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (enforced by zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every uses: pinned to a full commit SHA with checksums and attestations), and secret exposure in logs. See docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/build-assessment.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the project's security architecture: least privilege in workflows, an explicit capability boundary forbidding id-token: write in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency track conformance with written assurance in docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/release.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/0BSD.txt in the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the project REUSE-compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (0BSD) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt. `reuse lint` reports 141 of 141 files with licence information and api.reuse.software independently reports the project compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: releases are cut continuously from conventional commits, Renovate and Dependabot keep pins current, and a scheduled Monday audit re-checks settings drift, link liveness and badge truth.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Consumers pin this repository by tag or commit SHA and move at their own pace; MAINTENANCE.md documents the versioned surface, what a release means and what may change between versions, and Renovate opens the upgrade pull request for every consumer automatically. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
release_notes_justification: Every release carries generated release notes: CHANGELOG.md is produced by git-cliff from conventional commits and the same summary is attached to the GitHub release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release so far has fixed a publicly known run-time vulnerability that had a CVE assignment at the time. The changelog is generated from conventional commits, so a fix would appear in the notes for the release that carried it, and the dependency track additionally publishes VEX decisions keyed by package and version.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public and permanently archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted through GitHub Issues using the repository's issue forms; SUPPORT.md states where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed in the last 12 months has been acknowledged and triaged by the maintainer; the tracker carries no unanswered reports.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: Key roles are not documented as roles. CODEOWNERS routes review to an `owners` team and docs/continuity.md names succession and break-glass paths, but there is no document defining the roles themselves and what each is responsible for. It follows the same gap as `governance`.
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews written against this project's own security requirements and boundary, control by control, and docs/slsa-reference.md records what is claimed and what is deliberately not. They are current, not historical: the scheduled audit re-checks the claims they rest on. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
signed_releases_justification: Verified against the published release rather than asserted: v1.22.2 carries attestations.intoto.jsonl (the Sigstore evidence bundle) and checksums.txt alongside the archive and its SPDX SBOM. Signing is keyless — Sigstore/Fulcio with a Rekor transparency-log entry, no long-lived key — and docs/runbook.md documents verification from the consumer's position under 'Verifying as a consumer would'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/releases/tag/v1.22.2
sites_https_justification: The repository, its releases and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: The labels exist ('good first issue', 'help wanted') but no issue currently carries either, so in practice small tasks are not identified for a newcomer. Labelling the genuinely self-contained open items would close this.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: zizmor is a vulnerability scanner specific to what this project produces — GitHub Actions workflows — covering template injection, excessive permissions, credential persistence and unpinned actions. CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide and trivy adds misconfiguration and secret rules. All run in the gate on every pull request.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge — the gate blocks the pull request, so no finding of medium or higher severity has ever reached main unaddressed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and the gate additionally runs shellcheck over every tracked shell task, actionlint and zizmor over every workflow, and trivy over configuration — on every pull request, before any release.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, and a scheduled Monday audit re-runs the network-dependent checks.
test_policy_mandated_justification: The policy exists and is written in CLAUDE.md — new enforcement enters the belt as a `lint:*` task at maximum defensible enforcement — but it is not a formal written policy in the contribution instructions, and it speaks of checks rather than tests. Writing it into CONTRIBUTING.md is a small change and would close this and tests_documented_added together.
tests_are_added_justification: The most recent major changes each shipped their own gate task: lint:badges with the derived badge block, lint:licence with the licence policy, lint:citation with the derived CITATION.cff, and lint:capability-boundary with the id-token boundary rule.
tests_documented_added_justification: The documented instructions for change proposals (CONTRIBUTING.md) require that the gate pass but do not state that a change adding functionality must add the check that holds it. The practice is followed; the sentence is missing.
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, derived from conventional commits by git-cliff.
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified by an immutable git tag (v*), minted by the release App. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: The release tags are annotated tag objects minted by a GitHub App, and they are immutable under an organisation tag ruleset — but the tag objects themselves are not cryptographically signed (GitHub reports them 'unsigned'). Release integrity currently rests on the Sigstore evidence bundle, the artifact attestations and the signed source-provenance chain rather than on a tag signature. Signing the tag object is a real gap and is worth closing.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version, tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch> and minted by a GitHub App; tags are immutable under the org tag ruleset.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are identified; dependency updates are automated and the release gate blocks on the dependency checks.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity. Renovate and Dependabot open updates continuously, trivy runs in the gate, and the dependency track records VEX decisions keyed by package and version.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters who do not request anonymity.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
